elaine: Heads-up — after last night's runtime rollout (hybrid-attn kernel + new quant profile) we see a sustained drop in prefix-cache hit rate for a subset of traffic.  Drop started ~00:40 UTC and correlates with the deploy.
pranav: Saw the same in dashboards. global prefix hit went from ~78% -> ~63% on p99-prewarm paths. Not all models affected.
yuan: Which models? can you paste model ids and kernel flags?
elaine: Most affected: rdx-13b-v2 and a handful of rdx-7b variants that were routed to the hybrid-attn kernel. Kernel flag: hybrid_attn_v2=true, fused_matmul=false. Quant profile: q2_4_dynamic.
elaine: Quick sample from the webserver logs (trimmed):
```
2024-06-01T00:40:12Z INFO route=hosted model=rdx-13b-v2 kernel=hybrid_attn_v2 prewarm_hit=false cache_key=sha1:7f4e... latency=18ms
2024-06-01T00:40:12Z INFO route=hosted model=rdx-13b-v2 kernel=old_attn prewarm_hit=true cache_key=sha1:7f4e... latency=6ms
2024-06-01T00:40:15Z INFO route=hosted model=rdx-7b-q kernel=hybrid_attn_v2 prewarm_hit=false cache_key=sha1:3a1b... latency=22ms
```
pranav: The weird thing is the cache_key looks identical across kernels for the same prompt in other cases. Are we normalizing tokenization / attention masks differently in the hybrid path?
elaine: I diffed the keying code paths — we call prefix_normalize(token_ids, tokenizer_version) in both, but the hybrid-attn path also applies a per-seq padding normalization for kernel alignment. That might reorder trailing null tokens.
sam: Could reordering be changing the hashed key even if semantic content same? yes. Hashes are deterministic on byte sequence. Any change to serialization will flip keys.
yuan: Is this a recent change in the kernel that touches how the runtime pads or stores KV cache frames?
elaine: The hybrid-attn kernel uses packed KV buffers to optimize memory; to enable that we normalize seq padding to align to 8-token boundaries. The old path left original padding alone.
pranav: That explains the mismatch. But why only some traffic? maybe many clients already strip trailing padding or use shorter sessions so padding difference is invisible.
pranav: Quick profiling: when prewarm_hit=false we see extra 8–12ms spent in key_lookup path (likely recomputing canonicalization).
ci-bot: deploy:hybrid-attn-rollout completed by @infra at 2024-06-01T00:38:47Z :rocket:
yuan: Two immediate mitigations: 1) revert kernel change (rollback), or 2) make cache keying canonicalize after kernel-level padding to match hybrid path (i.e., canonicalize to packed representation everywhere).
sam: Option 2 seems safer long-term but we must ensure canonicalization cost is low. We could memoize canonicalization per-request and add a short-lived LRU in the webserver.
elaine: I ran a local microbench: canonicalizing to packed representation adds ~0.6ms median per-request but removes the extra 8–12ms downstream (net win), because it avoids full recompute of KV frames and avoids cache miss cold paths.
yuan: Are there any security or correctness concerns canonicalizing differently? e.g., user-visible outputs or eval diffs? It should be purely internal to keying; we must ensure we don't change model input stream semantics.
pranav: Another nuance — quant profile q2_4_dynamic changes some rounding for attention weights; could that affect deterministic fingerprinting if we included raw floats in key derivation anywhere?
sam: We do NOT include floats in the key. Keys are based on normalized token sequence + tokenizer version + model build id. But build id is different between quant profiles; are we including the runtime build id?
elaine: We include model_build_id. The problematic traffic had identical build id; so it's not that.
yuan: Plan: patch webserver to apply the packed-padding canonicalization before computing cache key, add micro-LRU for canonicalized serials (ttl 30s), and roll a canary. If canary looks good, roll globally. Also add an instrumentation flag to log canonicalization path.
pranav: +1. Can we ship the canary in the next canary lane and monitor prewarm_hit, tail latency, and CPU delta?
elaine: I'll push a PR with the keying shim and short-lived LRU. PR will include unit tests that ensure key equality across kernels and a perf benchmark.
elaine: PR link: https://git.redwood/rdx/runtime/pulls/1245 (contains bench results)
yuan: After canary, let's also run a mass rehash job to populate prefix cache for older entries? That might be costly. Alternatively, rely on warmup traffic to repopulate if latency is acceptable.
sam: Rehash job could spike IO. Recommendation: allow gradual warmup, and for high-SLA customers we can do targeted re-seeding for top N prompts.
pranav: Also add an alert for prewarm_hit drop + rollout tag to avoid silent future regresses.
elaine: Will add alert and rollout tag. Quick status: PR opened, canary scheduled for 02:15 UTC, rollback window 30m. Will update thread with canary metrics. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
